claims.claim: Consolidated Alphabet revenues for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 increased 24% to $119.8 billion.
Constant currency revenue growth was 23%.
Net income available to common stockholders rose 298% to $112.1 billion.
Diluted EPS was $9.11, compared with $2.31 in the prior-year quarter.
Operating income increased 30% to $40.8 billion.
Operating margin expanded by 2 percentage points to 34%.
Other income reflected a net gain of $98.0 billion, primarily driven by net unrealized gains on equity securities.
Google Services revenues grew 15% to $94.5 billion.
Google Services growth was supported by 17% growth in Google Search & other, 15% in Google subscriptions, platforms, and devices, and 13% in YouTube ads.
Google Cloud revenues accelerated significantly, increasing 82% to $24.8 billion.
Google Cloud growth was led by Google Cloud Platform enterprise AI Solutions, enterprise AI Infrastructure, and core services.
Alphabet-level activities primarily reflect shared AI research and development expenses.
Alphabet-level activities produced an operating loss of $5.8 billion, up from a $3.4 billion loss in the prior-year period.
The release does not provide specific financial guidance or outlook for future quarters.
The release notes that actual results may differ materially from forward-looking statements based on risks detailed in SEC filings.
In June 2026 the company issued Class A stock, Class C stock, and mandatory convertible preferred stock for aggregate net proceeds of $49.6 billion.
The $49.6 billion of equity proceeds are to be used to scale AI infrastructure.
claims.note: Acceptable paraphrase, though narrowed: the release says the proceeds are for general corporate purposes, including capital expenditures to scale AI infrastructure and global compute.

claims.claim: The company issued senior unsecured notes for net proceeds of $20.3 billion in the second quarter of 2026 for general corporate purposes.
As of June 30, 2026, total cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities stood at $242.5 billion.
Long-term debt increased to $98.2 billion from $46.5 billion at year-end 2025.
The release highlights that fluctuations in the value of equity investments could significantly contribute to the volatility of other income and expense in future periods.
Alphabet-level operating losses widened to $5.8 billion from $3.4 billion year over year because shared AI R&D costs increased.
claims.note: The loss figures are correct, but the causal attribution is not in the release. The release only says Alphabet-level activities 'primarily reflect expenses related to our shared AI research and development'; that bucket also includes corporate initiatives, philanthropy, corporate shared costs and certain fines and settlements, and no increase in AI R&D spend is stated or quantified.

claims.claim: Inventory levels more than quadrupled to $10.0 billion from $2.4 billion in the prior year period.
claims.note: Wrong period for the comparison base: the $2,439 million figure is the December 31, 2025 balance sheet column, not the prior-year period; the release discloses no June 30, 2025 inventory balance. The 'more than quadrupled' multiple is also arithmetic the release does not show.
